**My reasoning as this farmer:**

I have grown wheat and corn my whole life, as my father did. In Quzhou, everyone rotates winter wheat with summer maize — that is just what this land is for. The soil here is flat and good for it, the government supports it with subsidies, and I know these crops in my bones. I am 67 now, my back is not strong, my son is in Baoding. I cannot manage complicated things. I keep about 8 mu under cultivation — I gave up 3 mu two years ago because I could not keep up with it alone.

For wheat, I buy the improved seed from the village cooperative — Jimai series, the one everyone here uses. I hire the machine man to do rotary tillage in October before I plant. I will irrigate three times: once before winter sets in, once at jointing, once when the grain is filling. I put down compound fertilizer at planting and urea when the wheat returns in spring. I spray herbicide once in March and spray again for rust and aphids before it heads. I expect around 450 jin per mu, maybe a little less — I am not as careful as I was at 50.

For maize, I plant the hybrid seed right after wheat harvest in June — no time to till properly, I just use the seeder directly. I let rain do most of the irrigation work, but if August is dry I pump once. One pesticide spray for fall armyworm if I see it. I do not overthink maize.
